_comment: Defaults for the Bot Settings inputs AND server-internal tunables. The dashboard reads the top-level keys via GET /api/bot-config-defaults as each input's value when bot-config.json has none, and the server falls back to them when `getConfig` is asked for a value the user hasn't set. Top-level keys use the bot-config-v2 POSITION_KEYS / GLOBAL_KEYS names, so one string flows from this file → dashboard input → bot-config.json → bot reader. Nested groups (lowGasThresholds, residualCleanup, ilGuardRetry, throttleDoubling) are server-internal, with no Bot Settings input.
_ranges_comment: Each value's range is in setting-bounds.json, at the same key. An override outside it stops startup with a message naming the setting, range and value.
_gasDeferral_comment: Before a rebalance starts, its gas (chains.json → estimatedRebalanceGasUnits at the current gas price) is priced in USD and compared with the position's value. Above rebalanceGasDeferPct percent, the rebalance waits, and the bot looks again after gasDeferRetrySec seconds instead of its usual poll interval, until gas comes down or a rebalance goes through. Read by src/bot-cycle.js and src/bot-loop.js.
_moralisEnabled_comment: Whether the stored Moralis API key is used for price lookups. Separate from whether a key exists — turning this off stops the calls without discarding the key, which is what an operator wants when a quota runs out or when Moralis is simply slower than falling straight through to GeckoTerminal. The dashboard exposes it in the Moralis API Key dialog, disabled when no key is configured. Default true: a key nobody has toggled behaves as it always did.
_rpcAccess_comment: RPC access plumbing. NOT exposed in the Bot Settings UI and NOT in bot-config-v2 GLOBAL_KEYS — these are operator-tunable plumbing, not user settings, and should never need changing in normal operation. Override them in app-config/user-configurable/bot-config-defaults.json and restart. The two work as a pair: chunk size decides how many requests a scan produces, the interval decides how fast they leave. See docs/configuration.md § "RPC Request Pacing and Log Chunking".
_getLogsChunkSize_comment: Max block span per eth_getLogs / queryFilter call; RPC endpoints reject anything wider than their cap. The published limit is 10000 blocks: rpc-pulsechain.g4mm4.io enforces it exactly, answering JSON-RPC -32602 'eth_getLogs is limited to a 10000 block range', while rpc.pulsechain.com and rpc.pulsechain.box accept wider. Default 9000, 90% of it, is verified on all three, with headroom for an endpoint enforcing slightly under its published figure. Lower it if an endpoint rejects a query; the error names this key. Raising it cuts requests and scan time.
_globalRPCRequestRateInterval_comment: Minimum milliseconds between ANY two JSON-RPC requests leaving this process. Every request — reads, writes, getBlockNumber, eth_call, transaction submission — queues in src/rpc-request-manager.js and is released one at a time on this schedule, so the whole process shares one budget regardless of how many providers or concurrent scans are running. Default 222 (4.5/s = 45 requests per 10 seconds), which is 10% under the tightest published limit we know of (rpc.pulsechain.box free tier: 50 requests per 10 seconds = 5/s). Lowered from 250 (4/s, 20% under) on 2026-09-14 to buy ~12% scan throughput. The margin is set against the only documented ceiling: the other two endpoints publish no limit, and none has been measured, so widen this again at the first sign of an endpoint rejecting requests under load. Set 0 to disable pacing entirely (only sensible against a local node).
_rpcAllEndpointsDownPause_comment: How long, in milliseconds, to hold EVERY JSON-RPC request once every endpoint in chains.json → rpc.urls has failed (3600000, one hour). With nothing answering, sending more only hammers dead hosts and fills the log; the pause lets an outage pass, then resumes from the FIRST endpoint, so later failovers walk the list in its original order. The pause is absolute, rebalances and compounds included: an exemption is a hole the pause escapes through, and the request that matters most in an outage is the least likely to succeed. A rebalance halted between its liquidity removal and its mint leaves that position drained until the pause lifts. Enforced in src/rpc-request-manager.js, triggered from src/send-transaction.js. 0 disables it (the bot then retries dead endpoints continuously). Capped by the timer rule in setting-bounds.json.
_rpcFailoverRate_comment: When an RPC endpoint is deemed out of service. Every RPC outcome in the process, success or failure (reads, writes, gas estimates, pool-state and wallet-balance walks), is reported to decideIfCurrentRPCIsOutOfService in src/rpc-out-of-service.js, which moves off the endpoint only when the share of failures inside the window exceeds rpcFailoverRatePercentage. So one 502 does not retire an endpoint, and a reader that fails often can report every failure without deciding for everyone. Successes count: a rate needs a denominator. rpcFailoverRateDurationMinutes is in MINUTES; its ceiling in setting-bounds.json also caps the decider's memory, one small tally per second per endpoint, about 0.3 MB an hour each.
_rpcRetryOn429_comment: Backoff when an RPC endpoint answers HTTP 429. A 429 says this process is sending too fast, so the response is to wait rather than to move — moving carries the same request rate to the next endpoint and collects its 429 too. Delays in milliseconds, tried in order for a single refused request; the per-endpoint penalty doubles with each consecutive refusal and every request to that endpoint honours it, capped at rpcMax429PenaltyMs. Same figures the price sources use (src/price-source-backoff.js), kept separate because the two limits are unrelated. A 429 is still counted as a failure sample, which the rate threshold above makes safe.
_rpcFailoverStickyMs_comment: How long, in milliseconds, failover stays on the endpoint it moved to before reads go back to the first in chains.json → rpc.urls. One hour (3600000) rides out a sustained outage of the preferred endpoint without stranding the bot on a slower one after a blip. Once the list is exhausted, the outage pause (rpcAllEndpointsDownPauseMS) sets the deadline instead. Read by src/send-transaction.js.
_boundedRead_comment: The budget of a read someone is waiting on: pool state, which gates every poll cycle and a Manage click; the wallet balances behind the re-open check; and the balance read after a swap lands. Each endpoint in service is asked up to boundedReadAttemptsPerEndpoint times, waiting boundedReadRetryDelayMs before asking the same endpoint again but not before moving to another. A spent budget makes the read report itself unavailable, which the dashboard shows as a dialog; after a swap it fails the rebalance or compound, and no second swap of the same balance is sent. Other reads have no budget and retry until some endpoint answers. Read by src/rebalancer-pools.js, src/server-can-reopen.js and src/rebalancer-swap-balance.js. The delay is a timer setting (src/timer-bounds.js).
_feeDataLogIntervalMs_comment: How often, in milliseconds, the network's gas price is logged (3600000, one hour). Every send asks for it, so logging each would bury the log; --verbose logs every one. Read by src/bot-provider.js.
_historyScan_comment: How the pool's rebalance history is read from the chain. historyLookbackYears: how many years back the Transfer scan reaches, turned into blocks with the chain's blockTimeSec in chains.json; it never starts before the pool's creation. eventCacheTtlMs: how long a pool's event cache in app-data/scan-cache/ keeps its history after its last write (one year); docs/engineering.md, Rebalance Event Caches, says what writes it. poolScanReuseMs: how long a finished scan's result is handed to the next caller for the same pool and wallet instead of a new scan (one minute; 0 turns reuse off), so dashboard views opened together do not each start one. rebalancePairingWindowSec: the most seconds between an NFT leaving the wallet and a new one arriving for the two to count as one rebalance. Read by src/event-scanner.js, src/pool-scanner.js and src/position-history-scan-helpers.js.
_priceCacheTtl_comment: Price-source cache TTL in milliseconds (in-memory cache inside src/price-fetcher.js, gated by the idle-driven pause). Default 120_000 (2 min) — long enough to absorb the 300 s poll cadence but short enough that a real price move shows up promptly when something's looking. The dust-unit-price cache TTL is computed at module-load as priceCacheTtlMs * dustUnitPriceCacheMultiplier, so the integer-multiple constraint is structural (a runtime assertion guards against future hand-edits).
_moveCacheTtl_comment: Price-source cache TTL while inside a withFreshPricesAllowed scope (rebalance/compound). Default 4_000 ms (4 s) — short enough that any move-relevant price change shows up but long enough to collapse the rapid-fire burst that the rebalance pipeline triggers when multiple stages (gas gate, slippage estimate, PnL snapshot, etc.) each call fetchTokenPriceUsd for the same token. Without this, a single rebalance can hit each price source 4-6× for one token in a few seconds. See src/price-fetcher.js and src/price-fetcher-gate.js#inMove.
_pricePauseExceptionPollWindowMultiple_c: For the 'positionBalanced' Telegram alert: poll cycles between fresh-price fetches that bypass the idle price-lookup pause, one every checkIntervalSec × this seconds (50 minutes as shipped). Higher means less price-source load, slower band detection. Used only while that alert is enabled.
_positionBalanced_comment: The 'positionBalanced' Telegram alert. positionBalancedBandPct: how far from an even 50/50 split of the position's dollar value still counts as balanced, in points either side (2.5: token0 between 47.5% and 52.5% of the total). The alert fires each time the split enters that band. positionBalancedCooldownMs: the least time between two alerts for one position (1800000, 30 minutes), so a split wavering across the band's edge does not alert at every crossing. Read by src/telegram-notifications/balanced-notifier.js.
_rescanPricesRecentWindowDays_comment: Re-scan Prices → 'Limit to the last N days': how many days back that option reaches. Only the Per-Day P&L table is date-scoped, so the option comes only with the Per-Day checkbox; the route's other half re-values chain-wide totals, which need every NFT. Periods closed before the cutoff keep their dollars and only those inside it are re-read and re-priced, turning a minutes-long rebuild of a long rebalance chain into a quick fix for one bad recent price. An incomplete history ignores the window and rebuilds in full: a stored period does not record its NFT, so a partial rebuild cannot tell a gap from an old period. The checkbox label reads it from /api/bot-config-defaults.
_impermanentLossGuardPct_comment: Impermanent Loss Guard: the most a position may have lost, in percent, before the bot stops rebalancing it. In Bot Settings → Execution, per position. The hypothetical post-rebalance position (LP value plus the pool residual it would absorb, slippage excluded) is compared with the held NFT's USD value at its mint, and the rebalance is rejected when it falls more than this far below. Rebalance Now skips the check. The default, 15, is tight on purpose: the two sides are not alike. Rebalancing CRYSTALLIZES the loss: re-minting around the current price makes permanent a paper loss a recovery would have undone. Declining costs only fees the out-of-range position is mostly not earning, and fees are what would have to earn the loss back, which in a low-volume pool can outlast the position. So an ordinary drawdown still rebalances and a deep one is left to recover. The cost of tightness: a blocked position mints no new NFT and keeps its old baseline, so it stays blocked until its value is back within the Guard of that baseline. Retries: the ilGuardRetry group below.
_swapChunkCount_comment: When the aggregator refuses a full-size swap for price impact above the slippage setting, it is tried again through the aggregator in this many equal parts, since a smaller swap moves the route's price less. Other failures are not split: a route that fails whole fails in parts. Read by src/rebalancer-swap.js.
_minSwapAmountRaw_comment: The least amount worth swapping, in the token's smallest unit: a smaller swap is skipped, and a split whose parts would fall below it is not tried. Read by src/rebalancer-pools.js.
_slippageSuggestionMarginPct_comment: When a swap is refused for price impact above the slippage setting, the message suggests a slippage of that impact, rounded up to a tenth of a percent, plus this many points. Read by src/rebalancer-swap-impact.js.
_correctiveSwapMaxRounds_comment: The most corrective swaps one rebalance makes after its main swap. The main swap can move the pool's own price, leaving the coins off the new range's ratio; each round swaps the excess back and can move the price again, so the step repeats until the coins match, the excess is not worth its gas, or this many rounds have run, each paid for in gas and slippage. Read by src/rebalancer-correct.js.

throttleDoubling._comment: Doubling mode, the rebalance throttle's brake on a busy pool, starts when triggerCount rebalances land within triggerWindowMultiple times the Min Time Between Rebalances; from then on each rebalance doubles the wait before the next. It clears after a quiet spell of quietWindowMultiple times the current, doubled, wait, or at midnight UTC. Enforced by src/throttle.js; the dashboard's trigger window and help reflect any override of yours.

_rebalanceRangeWidthPct_comment: The Price Range Extension (percent of current price) that the Default button on that row (Bot Settings → Range) puts in the input. It is NOT applied to the bot on its own: a position with no saved value keeps its on-chain tick spread (preserveRange()), and the button only fills it in, to Save with one click. Raised from 15 to 80 from operator experience on PulseChain: a narrow band leaves range quickly, and each rebalance realizes impermanent loss and pays gas; a wider one earns a lower fee rate per unit of liquidity but leaves range far less often, the better trade in these markets.
_fullRangeRebalanceEnabled_comment: Per-position 'Full-Range Rebalance' toggle. When true, every rebalance mints at MIN_TICK / MAX_TICK via rangeMath.fullRange(), ignoring rebalanceRangeWidthPct. Driven by the 'Full-Range' checkbox next to the Price Range Extension input. A separate boolean rather than a rebalanceRangeWidthPct === 100 sentinel, because 100 is also a legal width.
_rangeOverrideEnabled_comment: Per-position 'No Override' toggle heading Bot Settings → Range. false = re-use the position's existing on-chain range on the next rebalance (badge 'Re-Use Existing Position Range'); the Price Range Extension, Full-Range and Position Offset fields are disabled and none of them is applied. true = apply them (badge 'Use Settings Below'). This literal is the default for a position that has never been configured. A slot saved before the toggle existed keeps its settings: src/range-override.js resolveRangeOverrideEnabled() derives true when the slot already carries rebalanceRangeWidthPct, fullRangeRebalanceEnabled=true, or offsetToken0Pct. The toggle is non-destructive — it never clears those keys.

lowGasThresholds._comment: Wallet low-gas detection tunables. Used by src/gas-monitor.js to compute two tiers for the Mission Control 'Gas Running Low' / 'Gas Critical' badge and matching Telegram alerts. Formula (chain-agnostic — gas opcodes are identical across EVMs): floor_gas_units = standardSendGas × worstCaseGasFactor (one worst-case rebalance); recommended_gas_units = floor_gas_units × safetyMultiplier × managedPositionCount. Native-token threshold = gas_units × live gasPrice. Tiers: 'ok' at balance ≥ recommended; 'low' at floor ≤ balance < recommended (amber static); 'critical' at balance < floor (blinking — next rebalance will likely fail with out-of-gas). worstCaseGasFactor=91 was derived from observed PulseChain rebalance_log.json + live logs (NFT #158965→158967) covering a rebalance that fired all 3 corrective-swap iterations: remove(~209k) + primary approve(~46k) + primary swap(~243k) + 3×corrective(approve+swap ~290k each = ~870k) + mint approves(~76k) + mint(~464k) ≈ 1,911,000 gas / 21,000 send ≈ 91. safetyMultiplier=3 is the user-specified headroom factor. standardSendGas=21000 is the EVM constant for a native-token transfer with no calldata. If the JSON is missing or malformed, gas-monitor falls back to these same defaults so the guard never silently disables.

ilGuardRetry._comment: Backoff between retries of a rebalance the Impermanent Loss Guard has rejected. First retry after baseMs (14400000 = 4 h), then doubling on each consecutive rejection — 4 h, 8 h, 16 h, 32 h — until it reaches maxMs (604800000 = 7 days), which it then holds. The ladder resets the moment the Guard lets a rebalance through, so a position that recovers starts again at 4 h. Same shape as the rebalance throttle's doubling mode. The Telegram alert rides the same schedule, so a position blocked for a long stretch reports on a widening interval rather than every poll. Cost: a position that recovers inside a window waits for it to expire; a manual 'Rebalance Now' ignores the backoff entirely. Not exposed in Bot Settings — operator-tunable via this file only.

residualCleanup._comment: Automatic residual-cleanup rebalance tunables. After every successful normal or manual rebalance, if the wallet residual share of the pool batch (residual / (LP + residual)) still exceeds thresholdPct past delayMs, the bot fires exactly one cleanup rebalance to sweep residuals back into the position. The cleanup respects ALL other rebalance rules (throttle, daily cap, doubling, swap-backoff, pause). Back-to-back cleanups are prevented by a per-position flag that only clears on the next normal rebalance. Not exposed in Bot Settings — operator-tunable via this file only.
